blocks.text: Neutrophils are a type of white blood cells. They use three methods for killing pathogens. The first method is phagocytosis. In the second method, they release soluble anti-microbial chemicals on pathogens. In the third method, they generate and release network of DNA fibres. These fibres bind with pathogenic bacteria and kill them.

blocks.alt: One neutrophil at the top, with three arrows to its three methods: phagocytosis (a pathogen taken into a pocket of the cell), release of anti-microbial chemicals (granules released onto a pathogen), and generation of a network of fibres that trap a pathogen.
blocks.caption: Figure 21.5: Methods of neutrophils to kill pathogens (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 21.5).
